rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.point: Constellation seeks rehearing of two final determinations: rejection of Eddystone-type eligibility and acceptance of mandatory price-taker treatment.
rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.quote: Constellation seeks rehearing of two final determinations in the Order.

rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.point: Energy-only resources that obtain new capacity interconnection rights should qualify as backstop resources, since they supply new deliverable capacity.
rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.quote: adequacy increment is new deliverable capacity available to PJM

rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.point: The order cited reliability-must-run precedent without a balancing analysis, though the backstop could place 6,831.3 MW of price-taker supply in auctions for up to fifteen years.
rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.quote: The RBP instead may place 6,831.3 MW of forecast-driven, separately compensated capacity into repeated RPM Auctions as price- taker supply for as long as fifteen years

rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.point: Constellation asks FERC to clarify that the collateral paper hearing covers the size and method of the RBP Credit Rate and related issues.
rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.quote: the paper hearing concerning appropriate collateral requirements for RBP buyers encompasses Constellation’s arguments concerning the size and methodology of the RBP Credit Rate

rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.point: Any replacement cost allocation must rest on current, PJM-validated load forecast data consistent with the procurement target.
rehearing-er26-3380-constellation.quote: The forecast used to establish the procurement target and the data used to allocate costs must be consistent or expressly reconciled.

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: FirstEnergy says the September 29 order accepts the RBP except three paper-hearing topics but does not answer its arguments on the rest.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: the September 29 Order accepts the filing, declares that every aspect of the RBP other than three discrete topics set for paper hearing is just and reasonable

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: FirstEnergy says the order suspended the RBP five months to February 28, 2027 and set a paper hearing on cost allocation, TO exit rules and LSE collateral.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: suspended them for five months to become effective February 28, 2027, subject to refund

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: FERC granted PJM's abeyance request, moving initial briefs to January 11, 2027 and reply briefs to January 26, 2027.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: extending the deadline for initial briefs in the paper hearing Docket No. EL26-108-000 from November 13, 2026 to January 11, 2027

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: The $555/MW-day cap is a levelized average, which FirstEnergy says lets sellers front-load prices into early years.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: sellers will front-load their costs into the initial years of their contracts.

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: It asks FERC to require firm, dispatchable resources to be prioritized, citing NERC reliability evidence.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: The Commission should grant rehearing and require PJM to demonstrate that the RBP framework appropriately prioritizes firm and dependable capacity resources.

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: Shortfall charges apply only before commercial operation, so customers lack protection against underperformance over the 15-year term.
LSEs post $1.5 million per RBP MW in collateral while sellers post only three years of shortfall charges.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: Customers are asked to post collateral of $1.5 million per committed RBP MW to protect suppliers for up to fifteen years

rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.point: It asks FERC to clarify that demand response must be backed by binding contractual commitments, not just a plan.
rehearing-er26-3380-firstenergy.quote: clarify that Demand Resources and DER Capacity Aggregation Resources must be supported by binding contractual commitments to provide the

rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.point: The Owners seek rehearing out of caution and hope PJM files a revised Section 205 proposal that moots it.
rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.quote: submit this rehearing request out of an abundance of caution to preserve their rights in this fast-moving and dynamic proceeding.

rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.point: FERC accepted the proposal, suspended it five months to February 28, 2027, and set a paper hearing on cost allocation, exit rules and collateral.
rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.quote: suspended for five months, effective February 28, 2027, subject to refund and the outcome of the further procedures ordered in this proceeding.

rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.point: The Order found PJM did not explain why transmission owners should bear backstop charges, but did not reject the exit fee outright.
rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.quote: fails to explain why Transmission Owners—who are not the buyers for which PJM procures capacity under the RBP—should be responsible for RBP Charges

rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.point: The Owners say the cost-causation finding should be final: transmission owners are not the beneficiaries of the backstop.
rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.quote: should have been stated finally and definitively, instead of being left open for decision after a paper hearing.

rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.point: PJM lacked filing authority because the Exit Amendment changes the Consolidated Transmission Owners Agreement, which needs a transmission owner vote.
rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.quote: PJM cannot avoid the CTOA’s amendment procedures by casting a change to the core terms of the CTOA as an amendment to the OATT, rather than to the CTOA.

rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.point: PJM also skipped the 45 days' notice owed to transmission owners and should have used Section 206.
rehearing-er26-3380-indicated-pjm-tos.quote: PJM therefore was required to provide the TOs with 45 days’ notice before filing the Exit Amendment.

rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.point: The advocates call the pay-as-bid design flawed because it permits seller-side market power and likely over-procures at high cost.
rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.quote: it permits the unmitigated exercise of seller-side market power and its design seems guaranteed to ensure that PJM procures more resources than are necessary, at costs higher than are warranted.

rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.point: The $555/MW-day cap is borrowed from a 2028/2029 BRA reference point that was replaced by a $325/MW-day collar, and would apply for up to 15 years.
rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.quote: price cap that is 70% higher and will be applied to commitment periods up to 15 times longer than was the case for the 2028/2029 BRA.

rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.point: They say the 15-year commitment could add about $13 billion of unneeded cost, since PJM says five years addresses the shortfall.
rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.quote: could unjustly and unreasonably saddle captive ratepayers with some $13 billion in excessive and unnecessary RBP costs.

rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.point: They say the Order does not engage the objection that the RBP has no locational constraints, noting up to 6,831 MW against 149 GW of existing supply.
rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.quote: the volume of capacity that PJM will procure through the RBP auction— up to 6,831 MW—is relatively small compared with total existing supply in PJM

rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.point: Resources chosen without regard to location could dilute BRA locational price signals for up to 15 years.
rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.quote: those resources will participate in the BRA as price takers and will thereby diminish the effect of the BRA’s locational price signals for up to 15 years.

rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.point: Relief requested: rehearing, a finding that four RBP elements are unjust and unreasonable, and directed changes in a later filing.
rehearing-er26-3380-joint-consumer-advoc.quote: find unjust and unreasonable the four elements of the RBP framework identified herein by Joint Consumer Advocates; and (3) direct PJM to incorporate changes to those elements

rehearing-er26-3380-novec.point: NOVEC says FERC never addressed its argument for the voluntary, stakeholder-endorsed subscription model.
rehearing-er26-3380-novec.quote: The Commission did not respond to or consider NOVEC’s argument, which advocated for the adoption of the voluntary framework as an alternative to the RBP filed by PJM.

rehearing-er26-3380-novec.point: Under the voluntary framework, developers could subscribe to pay backstop costs or accept an interruptible form of transmission service.
rehearing-er26-3380-novec.quote: interested developers would have the option to subscribe to pay the RBP costs or accept an interruptible form of transmission service.

rehearing-er26-3380-novec.point: NOVEC says the voluntary model was the only proposal endorsed in stakeholder discussions out of more than a dozen considered.
rehearing-er26-3380-novec.quote: The voluntary RBP framework achieved a clear consensus during stakeholder discussions as the only proposal endorsed out of more than a dozen considered.

rehearing-er26-3380-novec.point: The backstop charges only some LSEs based on the retail load they serve, which NOVEC calls undue discrimination.
rehearing-er26-3380-novec.quote: PJM has no authority to base its tariff rates and charges on the character of retail service provided by LSEs.

rehearing-er26-3380-novec.point: NOVEC says the capacity shortfall has causes beyond data centers, so cost allocation that ignores them breaks cost causation.
rehearing-er26-3380-novec.quote: the causes of the present shortfall pre-date and are not solely due to the buildout of data centers.

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: OCC says the accepted RBP design does not match concurrences by Commissioners LaCerte and See that new load, not existing customers, should bear its costs.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: Existing customers should not be left paying costs attributable to new demand.

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: The order accepted a one-time procurement of 6,831 MW and postponed the auction five months to February 28, 2027.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: it postponed that auction for five months, until February 28, 2027.

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: OCC lists the paper hearing topics FERC set: zonal cost allocation, muni and co-op opt-outs, TO exit fees and LSE collateral.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: set these issues for further paper hearings and additional comments

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: OCC says the $555/MW-day cap and pay-as-bid clearing lack record support and do not mitigate seller market power.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: There is no evidence in the record to support this offer cap, and there is no evidence to support the pay-as-bid clearing mechanism design.

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: It says the cap is more than $200/MW-day above the collared cap in the 2028/2029 base residual auction.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: more than $200/MW-day higher than the current collared price cap applied in the 2028/2029 RPM base residual auction.

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: OCC says the 20% shortage penalty is far below RPM's non-performance penalty and shortfall charges are limited to three years against a 15-year commitment.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: FERC accepted a proposal to limit the proposed shortage penalty to only 1/5th of the capacity sell offer

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: It says costs should fall on data centers and FERC ignored a claimed $23.1 billion cost shift from the past three auctions.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: data center demand increased capacity costs to other PJM customers by approximately $23.1 billion

rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.point: OCC's prayer asks FERC to lower the cap, adopt single clearing price, reject the 20% penalty and allocate RBP costs to cost causers.
rehearing-er26-3380-ohio-occ.quote: directing PJM to set a lower market seller offer cap for the RBP auction consistent with protests filed by OCC and others on this issue

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: PJM's Initial RBP Target is 6,831.3 MW of UCAP, the amount the 2028/2029 auction cleared short.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: PJM set the Initial RBP Target at 6,831.3 MW.

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: The September 29 order set paper hearing procedures on cost allocation, Transmission Owner exit rules and LSE collateral.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: The Commission established paper hearing procedures to address three aspects of the PJM Filing – cost allocation, Transmission Owner exit rules, and collateral requirements for Load Serving Entities

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: AMP first asks FERC to clarify that its suggested allocation method fails cost causation if it charges zones without large load growth.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: the Commission should clarify that it would not be just and reasonable to apply the Commission’s potential modification to PJM’s cost allocation method if it would result in RBP costs being allocated to Electric Distributor zone/areas that are not experiencing load growth attributable to data centers or other large loads

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: AMP second asks FERC to confirm that it made no final ruling on PJM's as-filed allocation method.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: The Commission should clarify that it has not made a final decision regarding the justness and reasonableness of PJM’s as-filed RBP cost allocation approach

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: AMP asks that parties may defend PJM's as-filed allocation in the paper hearing.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: The Commission should also clarify that parties may address PJM’s as-filed cost allocation proposal in the paper hearing procedures.

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: If clarification is denied, AMP seeks rehearing, calling the rejection arbitrary and capricious.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: The Commission’s rejection of PJM’s proposal was arbitrary and capricious, as it was based on an apparent misunderstanding of PJM’s approach.

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: AMP says PJM used Load Adjustments from Table B9b, which count large loads that Table B9 would miss.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: PJM, however, did not rely on the Load Adjustments shown in Table B9 to allocate RBP costs, it proposed to use the Load Adjustments in Table B9b of the Load Forecast.

clarification-er26-3380-amp.point: AMP says the lack of a MW threshold for Load Adjustments is now fixed with a 50 MW threshold in PJM Manual 19.
clarification-er26-3380-amp.quote: PJM Manual 19 has been updated to specify a 50 MW threshold for future Load Adjustments
